## CM6 Code Blocks: `view.dispatch()` replaces the OS-clipboard paste entirely (2 Sep, ERF homepage restructure)

The CM5 note above ("Two write paths that silently revert") killed the clipboard dance for
**Embed** blocks. This kills it for **Code Blocks** too, which is the bigger win - the CM6
clipboard route was the single most fragile thing in this file.

`.cm-content` has a `cmTile` property carrying the live CodeMirror 6 `EditorView`. Walk up
from `.cm-content` because the property sits on the element itself, not reliably on an
ancestor:

```js
let el = document.querySelector('.cm-editor .cm-content'), view = null;
for (let i = 0; i < 8 && el; i++, el = el.parentElement) {
  if (el.cmTile && el.cmTile.view) { view = el.cmTile.view; break; }
}
view.state.doc.toString();                                   // FULL source, not virtualised
view.dispatch({changes:{from:0, to:view.state.doc.length, insert:NEXT}});
```

**`view.state.doc.toString()` is the read route the whole "`.cm-content` is virtualised"
problem was working around.** It returns the complete document. Use it to read a block
before overwriting it - the rule against blind overwrites (structured data hides in these
blocks) is unchanged, this just makes obeying it cheap.

Measured on the homepage restructure: read 3668 chars, wrote 7018, `after === NEXT` exact
on the first attempt. No `clip.exe`, no `Control+A`/`Control+V`, no shared-clipboard race,
no stray-YouTube-URL failure mode.

**It writes through.** Unlike `cm.setValue()` on CM5, no `cm.save()` / backing-textarea sync
is needed - the transaction fires the same update path a real edit does, and a plain
`.click()` on `[data-test="frameToolbarSave"]` committed it. Verified from anonymous `curl`,
not from the editor.

**The payload has to travel inside the function source.** `evaluate_script`'s `args` takes
element uids only, so a large literal cannot be passed as an argument - it goes in the
function body as a template literal. Check the payload for backticks and `${` first; a
7KB HTML/CSS block normally has neither, and one that does needs escaping or the script
fails in a way that looks like a tool error.

**Guards worth keeping in the same call**, all cheap and all caught something at some point:
an idempotence check (`if (src.includes('<marker>')) return 'ALREADY PRESENT'`), a
source-sanity check (abort unless the OLD marker is present, so a mis-targeted block is
never overwritten), an exact `after === NEXT` assertion, and a count assertion when doing an
anchor replace rather than a whole-buffer write.

the editor still opens in the PARENT document. Closing it opens a second "Code Editor"
dialog rather than closing - read `[role="dialog"]` and close the innermost first. Check
